title: hosted-eip-pool-allocator-and-conditional-dns-shielding
author: Priya Singh
description: Context: Private control plane deployments occasionally experience noisy egress IP churn during AZ failovers and scale events that causes downstream firewall policy thrashing and Route53 flapping for delegated DNS. This PR implements a coordinated EIP reservation pool allocator with AZ-aware affinity plus a conditional DNS shielding layer (Route53 resolver rules + local conditional-forwarders) to reduce cross-account DNS churn during control plane subnet handoffs. Motivation: Reduce incident surface where control-plane rehoming produces new public EIPs and spikes DNS propagation, and provide a predictable rollback path by keeping a warm pool of pre-allocated EIPs per AZ and a DNS 'shield' that buffers resolver changes until routed endpoints are stable. What this changes (high level): 1) Terraform: adds terraform/modules/vpc/eip_pool_allocator module that creates per-AZ Elastic IP pools using tags and autoscaling-friendly lifecycle rules, a small Lambda-backed reconciler (optional) for cross-account allocation, and new output variables for egress_allocation_id. 2) Networking: introduces a new security group pattern for egress-proxy-allocators to restrict control plane instance egress to a narrow set of ports used by resolvers and healthchecks. 3) DNS shielding: uses Route53 Resolver rules + conditional forwarders in the installer bootstrap to stage DNS delegations behind a resolver alias until the control plane announces healthy endpoints. 4) Helm/Installer: adds values under charts/private-installer to toggle eip_pool_allocator (on/off), allocator_size_per_az, dns_shield_ttl and reconciliation_interval. 5) Upgrade and rollback: migration plan creates reserved EIPs and attaches them to placeholder ENIs; rollout attaches instances to reserved IPs via staged handoffs; rollback detaches new allocations and reattaches the previous ENI allocation. Implementation notes: - The allocator module is idempotent and uses tag-based claims to avoid race conditions. - We provide a 'dry-run' mode where EIPs are created but not bound; installer defaults to dry-run=true in non-production workspaces. - The Lambda reconciler is packaged as a small Go binary and only enabled when cross-account allocation is required (controlled by module var enable_reconciler). - DNS shielding implements a two-phase alias swap with staged resolver rule activation to avoid cache poisoning and sudden delegation flips. Testing: - Unit: terraform plan/apply in a test account with dry-run toggles, module unit tests for tag claim logic. - Integration: staged install in our perf-lab with 3 AZ topology; simulated AZ termination to validate reattach and DNS hold. - E2E: smoke test of control plane API endpoints, DNS resolution consistency, and egress IP stability under a simulated scale event. Security considerations: new IAM role for the reconciler with least privilege for EIP describe/allocate/associate and Route53 resolver rule updates. We added audit log hooks for all allocation operations and a retention policy for 90 days. Rollback plan: revert helm values toggles, run reconciler in cleanup mode to release claimed EIPs, and re-run installer with previous subnets mapping. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4123, INF-8812. Breaking changes: none by default; feature is opt-in and disabled on existing installs. Notes for operators: recommended allocator_size_per_az=4 for mid-sized clusters; set dns_shield_ttl=30s for low-latency workloads but increase for high-propagation environments.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Please add explicit backoff on the reconciler when DescribeAddresses returns throttling - otherwise we saw a transient throttling in staging.
Priya Singh (author): Added exponential backoff with jitter in reconciler loop and bump to IAM throttle metrics. Verified in perf lab.
Marta Lopez: The security group lock-down is good but we need an escape hatch for operator SSH debugging; propose a one-time admin-authorized ephemeral rule via our existing bastion workflow.
Priya Singh (author): Added --enable-ephemeral-admin flag to helm values and documented the operator workflow in docs/ops/eip_allocator.md.
Rahul Patel: Terraform plan shows potential drift on tag renaming if existing EIPs lack the new tag; ensure migration tolerates empty tags.
Priya Singh (author): Migration tolerates untagged EIPs; reconciler will claim untagged EIPs when dry-run=false and log events for operator review.
release_notes: Opt-in EIP pool allocator and DNS shielding for private control plane installs. Provides AZ-aware reserved EIP pools, optional reconciler for cross-account allocation, and staged Route53 resolver based DNS guard to reduce propagation churn. Configurable via helm.values eip_pool_allocator and dns_shield_ttl. Default disabled for existing installs.
